About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!

Owner’s acquisition engine first identifies what makes a given restaurant unique, evaluates local demand for its offerings, and assesses the most relevant competition to determine the best strategy for promoting that restaurant. Then, the platform automatically generates relevant website pages and content, monitors results over time, and evolves its strategy as it gets more data.



We are looking for a mission-driven engineer who is passionate about their craft and committed to building incredible products for our customers.

 - Own the technical strategy for SEO/AEO systems at scale, translating ambiguous growth goals into a prioritized roadmap, clear metrics, and durable system architecture.

 - Drive a rigorous experimentation and measurement loop, partnering with product, data, and cross-functional teams to validate impact, diagnose regressions, and continuously improve performance.

 - Mentor and multiply the team, setting engineering standards, reviewing designs, coaching other engineers, and aligning across teams where changes require shared ownership.



What we need:



 - Strong technical leadership and end-to-end ownership.
   
   Ability to set direction, drive alignment, and deliver multi-quarter initiatives from design through launch and iteration.

 - Familiarity with SEO systems at scale.
   
   Experience with crawling and indexing, content generation, templating, structured data, internal linking, canonicalization, and internationalization is a plus.

Compensation and benefits

We pride ourselves on our culture across engineering of engaging in thorough technical design review, operational excellence, and capable incident response and analysis.
 Affirm runs its workloads on more than 85 Amazon EKS clusters, and the number is growing. The Workload Safety team creates one set of standards for how workloads are configured and run, so Affirm can grow globally and still meet its availability and latency SLOs. The team identifies the industry best practices Affirm needs, drives their adoption across every engineering team on EKS, and enforces them through policy and automation so new workloads comply by default.
 As a senior engineer on the team, you will help set its roadmap, decide which standards matter most, and build a repeatable way to take each standard from research to enforcement across the fleet.
 What you’ll do 
 Define and evolve workload safety standards for Affirm's EKS fleet, such as CPU and memory settings, workload isolation and placement, tolerance for disruption, graceful termination to name a few
 Own each standard end to end: research and prototyping, white-glove onboarding for early adopters, self-service guidance for everyone else, and automation and policy guardrails that keep every workload compliant from day one
 Lead cross-team initiatives from design through fleet-wide rollout, mentor other engineers, and set a high bar for design, code review, and operational readiness
 Isolate workloads by criticality and resource profile so one misbehaving workload cannot degrade critical paths such as checkout
 Fix stuck workloads and node lifecycle problems, such as pods that ignore termination signals, pod disruption budgets that block node cycling, and Karpenter timeouts that prevent bin packing and the removal of excess capacity
 Determine the safe operating limits of each cluster (pod count, node count, API server request volume), keep clusters within them, and develop control plane scaling patterns for bursty workloads such as scheduled batch jobs and large deployments
 Analyze workload resource profiles across the fleet (CPU, memory, disk, network) to guide EC2 instance type strategy, and automate that analysis as workloads change
 Measure each standard's impact on availability, latency, risk, and cost, and use the results to prioritize the roadmap
 Participate in on-call for Kubernetes runtime issues across the fleet, and turn recurring failure patterns into roadmap items
 Work closely with the teams that run services, batch jobs, and ML workloads on EKS, and with the deployment, capacity, and SRE teams
 Keep up with new best practices from the Kubernetes community and adapt them to Affirm's needs
 What we look for 
 5+ years of experience running Kubernetes in production at scale, ideally Amazon EKS across many clusters
 Deep understanding of Kubernetes resource management and scheduling: requests and limits, OOM and CPU throttling behavior, affinity and anti-affinity, taints and tolerations, and topology spread constraints
 Solid grasp of the pod lifecycle and disruption management, including graceful termination, pod disruption budgets, and node draining
 Experience enforcing configuration standards through admission control and policy-as-code (for example, OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno)
 Proficiency in Go or Python, including building production infrastructure software such as Kubernetes controllers, operators, or admission webhooks
 Strong production debugging skills and a demonstrated ability to turn recurring incidents into systemic fixes
 Track record of leading technical initiatives across multiple teams, driving adoption of shared standards, and mentoring other engineers
 Experience quantifying the impact of infrastructure changes on availability, latency, and cost
